items.stem: Why does comparing two String variables with == sometimes give an unexpected result in Java?

options.text: == compares object references, not the character contents
options.rationale: Correct: == tests reference identity; equals compares the character contents.

options.text: == is not a valid operator for any type in Java
options.rationale: == is valid; it compares references for objects and values for primitives.

options.text: Strings cannot be compared in Java at all
options.rationale: Strings can be compared, using equals or compareTo.

options.text: == automatically converts both Strings to integers
options.rationale: No such conversion happens; == does not parse Strings.

items.explanation: Correct: == tests reference identity; equals compares the character contents.

items.stem: Which statements about Java methods are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A method can be overloaded by changing its parameter list
options.rationale: Correct: overloading distinguishes methods by their parameter lists.

options.text: Primitive arguments are passed by value, so the method gets a copy
options.rationale: Correct: primitives are copied, so changes inside the method do not affect the caller's variable.

options.text: A void method must return a value
options.rationale: A void method returns nothing by definition.

options.text: Two methods with the same name and same parameters are allowed
options.rationale: Methods must differ in name or parameter list; identical signatures clash.

items.explanation: Correct: overloading distinguishes methods by their parameter lists.

items.stem: A checked exception in Java must be either caught or declared. What does this mean for a method that calls code throwing IOException?

options.text: The method must catch IOException or declare it with throws
options.rationale: Correct: checked exceptions must be handled or declared in the method signature.

options.text: The method will not compile under any circumstances
options.rationale: It compiles once the exception is caught or declared.

options.text: IOException is ignored automatically at runtime
options.rationale: Checked exceptions are not ignored; the compiler enforces handling.

options.text: The method must convert it to a RuntimeException first
options.rationale: Conversion is optional, not required, to satisfy the compiler.

items.explanation: Correct: checked exceptions must be handled or declared in the method signature.
